literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao, he was confined at the Imperial Secretariat.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianbao, Gao Longzhi was confined at the Imperial Secretariat.

literal: Longzhi had once feasted and drunk with Yuan Chang; when the wine was deep, he told Chang, "In friendship with Your Highness, one should never turn one's back, in life or in death.
idiomatic: Longzhi had once feasted with Yuan Chang; when the wine was deep, he told him, "In friendship with Your Highness, we should never turn our backs on each other, in life or in death.

literal: " Someone reported this in secret.
idiomatic: " Someone reported this in secret.

literal: Moreover, before the emperor had ascended the throne, Longzhi's bearing had often been contemptuous toward the emperor.
idiomatic: Moreover, before the emperor had ascended the throne, Longzhi's bearing had often been contemptuous toward him.

literal: When the emperor was about to receive the abdication from Wei, the ministers all said it was not yet permissible, and Longzhi was among them.
idiomatic: When the emperor was about to receive the abdication from Wei, the ministers all said it was not yet permissible — and Longzhi was among them.

literal: The emperor deeply resented this.
idiomatic: The emperor deeply resented this.

literal: For this reason he flew into a great rage and ordered brawny men to beat him more than a hundred blows.
idiomatic: For this reason he flew into a great rage and ordered brawny men to beat Longzhi more than a hundred blows.

literal: He was released; parched, he was about to drink water, but people stopped him. Longzhi said, "What does today matter!
idiomatic: He was released. Parched, he was about to drink water, but people stopped him. Longzhi said, "What does today matter!

literal: " And he drank.
idiomatic: " And he drank.

literal: He then followed the imperial procession and died on the road, aged sixty-one.
idiomatic: He then followed the imperial procession and died on the road. He was sixty-one.

literal: Posthumously granted authority over military affairs in the five provinces Ji, Ding, Ying, Cang, and You; grand general; grand tutor; grand guardian; governor of Ji Province; Prince of Yangxia.
idiomatic: He was posthumously granted authority over military affairs in the five provinces Ji, Ding, Ying, Cang, and You, made grand general, grand tutor, and grand guardian, and enfeoffed prince of Yangxia with governorship of Ji Province.

literal: In the end he was never granted a posthumous epithet.
idiomatic: In the end he was never granted a posthumous epithet.

literal: Although Longzhi had not studied, he admired and honored literary refinement; among gentry and eminent men he always treated them with courtesy.
idiomatic: Although Longzhi had not studied, he admired literary refinement; among gentry and eminent men he always treated them with courtesy.

literal: An elder sister had become a nun; he served her as a mother would and, in instructing his sons, always put literary principles first.
idiomatic: An elder sister had become a nun; he served her as a mother would and, in instructing his sons, always put literary principles first.

literal: The age widely praised him for this.
idiomatic: The age widely praised him for this.

literal: In the late years of Xianzu, when suspicion and harm were many, he turned his wrath on Longzhi and executed more than ten of Longzhi's sons, including Deshu, casting them all into the Zhang River.
idiomatic: In Xianzu's late years, when suspicion and harm were many, he turned his wrath on Longzhi and executed more than ten of Longzhi's sons, including Deshu, casting them all into the Zhang River.

literal: He also opened Longzhi's tomb and took out the corpse; though it had been buried for years, the face was unchanged. The bones were hacked apart and likewise cast into the Zhang River, and the line ended.
idiomatic: He also opened Longzhi's tomb and took out the corpse; though it had been buried for years, the face was unchanged. The bones were hacked apart and likewise cast into the Zhang River, and the line ended.

literal: In Ganming, an edict made his elder brother's son Ziyuan Longzhi's heir, granting succession to the title Prince of Yangxia and restoring his property.
idiomatic: In Ganming, an edict made his elder brother's son Ziyuan Longzhi's heir, granting succession to the title prince of Yangxia and restoring his property.

literal: Earlier, when Longzhi had enjoyed the Grand Ancestor's trust, his nature was deeply malicious; no grudge, however small, went unavenged.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Longzhi had enjoyed Gao Huan's trust, his nature was deeply malicious; no grudge, however small, went unavenged.

literal: Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators Cui Xiaofen, because a marriage alliance failed; Grand Steward Ren Ji, who jointly managed construction and often clashed with him; and Ying Province governor Yuan Yan, whose requests went unfulfilled — Longzhi, one after another, fabricated crimes against them, and all were executed.
idiomatic: Commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators Cui Xiaofen, because a marriage alliance failed; grand steward Ren Ji, who jointly managed construction and often clashed with him; and Ying Province governor Yuan Yan, whose requests went unfulfilled — Longzhi, one after another, fabricated crimes against them, and all were executed.

literal: In the end his own house was wiped out; commentators called it retribution.
idiomatic: In the end his own house was wiped out; commentators called it retribution.

literal: Sima Ziru, styled Zunye, was a native of Wen in Henei.
idiomatic: Sima Ziru, styled Zunye, was a native of Wen in Henei.

literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Mo was Jin Minister of Works and Prince of Nanyang.
idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Mo was Jin minister of works and prince of Nanyang.

literal: Mo's heir Bao, in the chaos of Jin, fled to Liang Province and settled there.
idiomatic: Mo's heir Bao, in the chaos of Jin, fled to Liang Province and settled there.

literal: When Wei pacified Guliang, the family moved to Yunzhong — so runs their own account.
idiomatic: When Wei pacified Guliang, the family moved to Yunzhong — so runs their own account.

literal: His father Xinglong served as Wei governor of Luyang.
idiomatic: His father Xinglong served as Wei governor of Luyang.

literal: Ziru from youth was quick-witted and had a gift for speech.
idiomatic: Ziru from youth was quick-witted and had a gift for speech.

literal: He loved to befriend bold heroes and formed a deep bond of mutual trust with the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: He loved to befriend bold heroes and formed a deep bond of mutual trust with Gao Huan.

literal: In Xiaochang, when the northern provinces fell, Ziru led his household south to Si Province and was treated with honor by Erzhu Rong, who made him acting commander of the middle army.
idiomatic: In Xiaochang, when the northern provinces fell, Ziru led his household south to Si Province and was treated with honor by Erzhu Rong, who made him acting commander of the middle army.

literal: When Rong marched on Luoyang, Ziru was made marshal, given credentials, and appointed acting General Who Pacifies the South, supervising the vanguard.
idiomatic: When Rong marched on Luoyang, Ziru was made marshal, given credentials, and appointed acting general who pacifies the south, supervising the vanguard.

literal: At Gaodu, Rong, because Jianxing was rugged and lay on a vital route with worries for the rear, made Ziru acting governor of Jianxing and commander of that commandery.
idiomatic: At Gaodu, Rong — because Jianxing was rugged and lay on a vital route with worries for the rear — made Ziru acting governor of Jianxing and commander of that commandery.

literal: At the beginning of Yongan he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingyao County with a fief of three hundred households and continued as director in the Grand Mobilization Office.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongan he was enfeoffed baron of Pingyao County with a fief of three hundred households and continued as director in the Grand Mobilization Office.

literal: Rong, because Ziru was clear in argument and could speak to the affairs of the time, often sent him on missions to court, where he mostly pleased the throne; Emperor Xiaozhuang also received him warmly.
idiomatic: Rong, because Ziru was clear in argument and could speak to the affairs of the time, often sent him on missions to court, where he mostly pleased the throne; Emperor Xiaozhuang also received him warmly.

literal: When Ge Rong's rebellion broke out and Xiang Province stood isolated and perilous, Rong sent Ziru by secret route into Ye to help strengthen its defense.
idiomatic: When Ge Rong's rebellion broke out and Xiang Province stood isolated and perilous, Rong sent Ziru by secret route into Ye to help strengthen its defense.

literal: When Ge Rong was pacified, his rank was advanced to marquis.
idiomatic: When Ge Rong was pacified, his rank was advanced to marquis.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and hearts were divided and obstructed, because Ziru had once held Ye and had some grace and trust there, he was ordered to administer Xiang Province.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and hearts were divided, because Ziru had once held Ye and had some grace and trust there, he was ordered to administer Xiang Province.

literal: When Hao was pacified, he was summoned as Minister of Splendid Honors.
idiomatic: When Hao was pacified, he was summoned as minister of splendid honors.

literal: When Erzhu Rong was executed, Ziru knew there had been a coup; he burst out from within the palace, went to Rong's residence, abandoned his household, and followed Rong's wife and children with Erzhu Shilong and others in fleeing the capital.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong was executed, Ziru knew there had been a coup. He burst out from within the palace, went to Rong's residence, abandoned his household, and followed Rong's wife and children with Erzhu Shilong and others in fleeing the capital.

literal: Shilong wished at once to return north, but Ziru said, "In affairs, what matters is seizing the moment; in war, deception is not to be despised. The realm is in uproar — all look only to strength. At a juncture like this, one cannot show weakness.
idiomatic: Shilong wished at once to return north, but Ziru said, "In affairs, what matters is seizing the moment; in war, deception is not to be despised. The realm is in uproar — all look only to strength. At a juncture like this, one cannot show weakness.

literal: If we must flee north, I fear upheaval will follow at once. Better to divide the army to hold Heqiao, turn the host back toward the capital, and strike where they do not expect it — perhaps we can break and scatter them.
idiomatic: If we must flee north, I fear upheaval will follow at once. Better to divide the army to hold Heqiao, turn the host back toward the capital, and strike where they do not expect it — perhaps we can break and scatter them.

literal: Even if it does not go as we wish, it will still show that we have strength to spare and make the realm look on in fear of our might.
idiomatic: Even if it does not go as we wish, it will still show that we have strength to spare and make the realm look on in fear of our might.

literal: " Thereupon Shilong turned back and pressed on the capital.
idiomatic: " Thereupon Shilong turned back and pressed on the capital.

literal: When the Northern Wei Changguang King was enthroned, Ziru was additionally made Vice Director of the Left in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: When the Northern Wei Changguang King was enthroned, Ziru was additionally made vice director of the left in the Secretariat.

literal: The Deposed Emperor made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Cavalry General, and Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators, advancing his enfeoffment to Duke of Yangping Commandery with a fief of one thousand seven hundred households.
idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor made him attendant-in-ordinary, grand cavalry general, and commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators, advancing his enfeoffment to duke of Yangping Commandery with a fief of one thousand seven hundred households.

literal: He firmly declined the protocol rank and would not accept it.
idiomatic: He firmly declined the protocol rank and would not accept it.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous banner at Xindu, Shilong and the others, knowing Ziru had old ties with the Grand Ancestor, were suspicious and sent him out as governor of Nanqi Province.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous banner at Xindu, Shilong and the others, knowing Ziru had old ties with Gao Huan, were suspicious and sent him out as governor of Nanqi Province.

literal: Ziru, resentful and indignant, wept and pleaded his case, but could not escape removal.
idiomatic: Ziru, resentful and indignant, wept and pleaded his case, but could not escape removal.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor entered Luoyang, Ziru sent envoys to offer congratulations and again recalled their lifelong old kindness.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, Ziru sent envoys to offer congratulations and again recalled their lifelong old kindness.

literal: Soon he was summoned to the capital and made Director in the Grand Mobilization Secretariat, attending day and night at the Grand Ancestor's side and taking part in military and state affairs.
idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to the capital and made director in the Grand Mobilization Secretariat, attending day and night at Gao Huan's side and taking part in military and state affairs.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was made Vice Director of the Left and, together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Yue, Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Teng, and Vice Director of the Right Gao Longzhi, jointly managed court affairs; he was greatly trusted and honored.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was made vice director of the left and, together with attendant-in-ordinary Gao Yue, attendant-in-ordinary Sun Teng, and vice director of the right Gao Longzhi, jointly managed court affairs; he was greatly trusted and honored.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor held Jinyang, Ziru would from time to time go to audience; he was treated with great kindness — they sat together and ate from morning until evening. When it was time for him to return, the Grand Ancestor and Empress Wuming both sent gifts; this became the rule.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan held Jinyang, Ziru would from time to time go to audience and was treated with great kindness — they sat together and ate from morning until evening. When it was time for him to return, Gao Huan and Empress Wuming both sent gifts; this became the rule.

literal: Ziru's nature was bold and openhanded; relying moreover on old favor, in ledger affairs he granted and withheld as he pleased, openly accepting bribes without the least scruple.
idiomatic: Ziru's nature was bold and openhanded; relying moreover on old favor, in ledger affairs he granted and withheld as he pleased, openly accepting bribes without the least scruple.

literal: In Xinghe he was made commissioner of the Northern Circuit, inspecting the various provinces; prefects and magistrates and all below were subject to his promotions and demotions.
idiomatic: In Xinghe he was made commissioner of the Northern Circuit, inspecting the various provinces; prefects, magistrates, and all below were subject to his promotions and demotions.

literal: When Ziru reached Ding Province, he beheaded the magistrate of Shenze County;
idiomatic: When Ziru reached Ding Province, he beheaded the magistrate of Shenze County;

literal: when he reached Ji Province, he beheaded the magistrate of Dongguang County.
idiomatic: when he reached Ji Province, he beheaded the magistrate of Dongguang County.

literal: Both had delayed their reports past the deadline, and for this he inflicted the utmost penalty.
idiomatic: Both had delayed their reports past the deadline, and for this he inflicted the utmost penalty.

literal: If someone's words on promotion or demotion fell even slightly short of his wish, he would order brawny men to drag him down and set a naked blade at his neck.
idiomatic: If someone's words on promotion or demotion fell even slightly short of his wish, he would order brawny men to drag him down and set a naked blade at his neck.

literal: Gentry and commoners alike were terrified and did not know what to do.
idiomatic: Gentry and commoners alike were terrified and did not know what to do.

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Secretariat.

literal: From the first raising of the righteous banner, Ziru had taken no part in it; relying solely on being the Grand Ancestor's old friend, he yet held heavy responsibility. His spirit was very high, and he amassed wealth without cease.
idiomatic: From the first raising of the righteous banner, Ziru had taken no part in it; relying solely on being Gao Huan's old friend, he yet held heavy responsibility. His spirit was very high, and he amassed wealth without cease.

literal: At that time Shizong was assisting in court governance and inwardly came to dislike him; soon he was impeached for graft by Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian and confined at the Imperial Secretariat.
idiomatic: At that time Shizong was assisting in court governance and inwardly came to dislike him; soon he was impeached for graft by censor-in-chief Cui Xian and confined at the Imperial Secretariat.

literal: An edict pardoned him from the capital crime and stripped his office and rank.
idiomatic: An edict pardoned him from the capital crime and stripped his office and rank.

literal: Before long he was restored to administer Ji Province.
idiomatic: Before long he was restored to administer Ji Province.

literal: Ziru was able to discipline himself and reform; he gained a fine reputation, exposing fraud and deceit, and his subordinate officials feared and submitted to him.
idiomatic: Ziru was able to discipline himself and reform; he gained a fine reputation, exposing fraud and deceit, and his subordinate officials feared and submitted to him.

literal: He was transferred to administer Bing Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to administer Bing Province.

literal: An edict restored his office and rank; separately he was enfeoffed Baron of Yewang County with a fief of two hundred households.
idiomatic: An edict restored his office and rank; separately he was enfeoffed baron of Yewang County with a fief of two hundred households.

literal: His son Xiaonan succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Xiaonan succeeded.

literal: He married the Grand Ancestor's daughter; as imperial son-in-law and a nobleman's heir, he repeatedly served as director in the Secretariat and as gentleman in the Yellow Gate Office and as Vice Director of Splendid Honors.
idiomatic: He married Gao Huan's daughter; as imperial son-in-law and a nobleman's heir, he repeatedly served as director in the Secretariat, as gentleman in the Yellow Gate Office, and as vice director of splendid honors.

literal: He went out as governor of Northern Yu Province and garrisoned Wulao.
idiomatic: He went out as governor of Northern Yu Province and garrisoned Wulao.

literal: Xiaonan was broadly read in histories and records and had a fine presence, yet he could not be clean and honest; in the province he was impeached by the censorate.
idiomatic: Xiaonan was broadly read in histories and records and had a fine presence, yet he could not be clean and honest; in the province he was impeached by the censorate.

literal: Moreover he was on bad terms with the princess; the princess slandered and accused him. Fearing punishment, he then drew in neighboring enemies and fled to Guanxi.
idiomatic: Moreover he was on bad terms with the princess; the princess slandered and accused him. Fearing punishment, he then drew in neighboring enemies and fled to Guanxi.

literal: Ziru's elder brother Zuan had died earlier; when Ziru rose high, Zuan was posthumously made governor of Yue Province.
idiomatic: Ziru's elder brother Zuan had died earlier; when Ziru rose high, Zuan was posthumously made governor of Yue Province.

literal: Zuan's eldest son Shiyun was reckless and without proper conduct; he rose in succession to guard general and governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: Zuan's eldest son Shiyun was reckless and without proper conduct; he rose in succession to guard general and governor of Ying Province.

literal: Shiyun by origin had no merit; relying solely on being Ziru's nephew, he repeatedly held provincial and commandery posts.
idiomatic: Shiyun by origin had no merit; relying solely on being Ziru's nephew, he repeatedly held provincial and commandery posts.

literal: Relying on his uncle's power, wherever he served he amassed wealth and still indulged in wickedness and corruption.
idiomatic: Relying on his uncle's power, wherever he served he amassed wealth and still indulged in wickedness and corruption.

literal: When he was about to be prosecuted, inwardly he was alarmed and afraid; when Hou Jing rebelled, he then raised the province and followed him.
idiomatic: When he was about to be prosecuted, inwardly he was alarmed and afraid; when Hou Jing rebelled, he then raised the province and followed him.

literal: At that time Shiyun's younger maternal brother was in Ye; he gave his heart wholly to Jing and no longer looked back.
idiomatic: At that time Shiyun's younger maternal brother was in Ye; he gave his heart wholly to Jing and no longer looked back.

literal: When the generals besieged Jing at Yingchuan, Shiyun from atop the walls shouted across at the generals, his words very insolent.
idiomatic: When the generals besieged Jing at Yingchuan, Shiyun from atop the walls shouted across at the generals, his words very insolent.

literal: Shizong still, for Ziru's old kindness, pardoned his younger brothers from the death penalty and exiled them to the northern frontier.
idiomatic: Shizong still, for Ziru's old kindness, pardoned his younger brothers from the death penalty and exiled them to the northern frontier.

literal: After Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang, Shiyun again harbored a different intent and was killed by Jing.
idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang, Shiyun again harbored a different intent and was killed by Jing.

literal: Shiyun's younger brother Yingzhi, styled Zhongqing.
idiomatic: Shiyun's younger brother Yingzhi, styled Zhongqing.

literal: From youth he loved learning and had a fine bearing.
idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and had a fine bearing.

literal: In Tianping, when Ziru was at the height of power, Yingzhi rose from gentleman in the Secretariat through the Secretariat and the Yellow Gate Office.
idiomatic: In Tianping, when Ziru was at the height of power, Yingzhi rose from gentleman in the Secretariat through the Secretariat and the Yellow Gate Office.

literal: Ziru had been separately enfeoffed Duke of Xuchang County and transferred that title to Yingzhi.
idiomatic: Ziru had been separately enfeoffed duke of Xuchang County and transferred that title to Yingzhi.

literal: Yingzhi's household was rich in wealth and he enriched himself generously.
idiomatic: Yingzhi's household was rich in wealth and he enriched himself generously.

literal: Men such as Wang Yuanjing and Xing Zicai, because of long-standing esteem, held him in high regard.
idiomatic: Men such as Wang Yuanjing and Xing Zicai, because of long-standing esteem, held him in high regard.

literal: Because he was blunt and proud toward others, through the Tianbao reign he languished without rank.
idiomatic: Because he was blunt and proud toward others, through the Tianbao reign he languished without rank.

literal: In Ganming, Wang Xi reported to Emperor Suzong and had him made Vice Director of the Court of Guard.
idiomatic: In Ganming, Wang Xi reported to Emperor Suzong and had him made vice director of the Court of Guard.

literal: At the end of Heqing he was Minister of Splendid Honors.
idiomatic: At the end of Heqing he was minister of splendid honors.

literal: He suffered from dysentery and for years could not rise; by Wuping he still could not attend court audience, and at home he was invested Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: He suffered from dysentery and for years could not rise; by Wuping he still could not attend court audience, and at home he was invested commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators.

literal: He loved to read the Classic of Supreme Mystery and annotated Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Capital of Shu.
idiomatic: He loved to read the Classic of Supreme Mystery and annotated Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Capital of Shu.

literal: He would often say, "I wish to keep company with Yang Ziyun.
idiomatic: He would often say, "I wish to keep company with Yang Ziyun.

literal: " In the year Qi fell he died of his illness, aged seventy-one.
idiomatic: " In the year Qi fell he died of his illness. He was seventy-one.

literal: Yingzhi's nephew Zirui, in Tianbao served as chief administrator of Ding Province and was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: Yingzhi's nephew Zirui, in Tianbao served as chief administrator of Ding Province and was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

literal: He was recommended for integrity, diligence, fairness, and restraint.
idiomatic: He was recommended for integrity, diligence, fairness, and restraint.

literal: He was transferred to Left Director in the Department of State and concurrently Director of the Court of Judicatory, and was known for fairness and uprightness.
idiomatic: He was transferred to left director in the Department of State and concurrently director of the Court of Judicatory, and was known for fairness and uprightness.

literal: At the beginning of Ganming he held the post of Censor-in-Chief; with stern countenance he investigated and impeached, and the court approved him.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Ganming he held the post of censor-in-chief; with stern countenance he investigated and impeached, and the court approved him.

literal: He left office because of illness and was invested at home as Minister of Sacrifices.
idiomatic: He left office because of illness and was invested at home as minister of sacrifices.

literal: When he died, he was posthumously made governor of Ying Province with the posthumous epithet Wenjie.
idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made governor of Ying Province with the posthumous epithet Wenjie.

literal: Zirui's younger brother Youzhi was pure and upright, with established virtue; from youth he repeatedly held eminent posts.
idiomatic: Zirui's younger brother Youzhi was pure and upright, with established virtue; from youth he repeatedly held eminent posts.
